context: Switches the Kafka producer wrapper from blocking IDisposable cleanup to proper async disposal.
explanation: Safe to merge. The previous Dispose() blocked a thread on FlushAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult(), which risks a deadlock if a synchronization context is present and always wastes a thread waiting on I/O. DisposeAsync awaits the flush without blocking, still disposes the underlying producer, and calls GC.SuppressFinalize(this) as recommended for types implementing IAsyncDisposable. Callers switch to `await using`, which is the correct pattern for an async-cleanup resource.
